Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a clean redline of the MSA focused on the sections you flagged: output ownership, downstream productization, and the training/feedback license carve-outs. Two pragmatic asks up front so we can align the internal stakeholders: 

1) Can QuantaWorks confirm whether the primary requirement is an explicit "no training" carve-out for customer data (i.e., Redwood is prohibited from using any customer prompts/outputs to improve model weights) or a narrower "no retention/derivative training" promise limited to customer-provided confidential data?

2) What's your timeline for legal signoff? We have a requested production date in mid-Oct; if QW legal needs more time, we can gate go-live or push to a staged rollout.

Attached: QW_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (redline focused on Sections 4, 7, and 9) and a short redline_summary.xlsx with proposed language alternatives (A/B/C). Key highlights in the doc:
- Proposed language for an explicit "training opt-out" (Section 7.2.A) that preserves telemetry and non-identifying telemetry for service improvement but prohibits model weight updates from customer prompt/output pairs unless a separate training agreement is executed.
- Feedback license: we suggest a narrow, non-exclusive license to use customer feedback for service quality improvement (metrics/bug fixes) but not for model retraining.
- Output assignment: offer a carveout for customer-generated content used in customer-facing product features (i.e., QW retains downstream product rights) while Redwood retains system-level rights for analytics/aggregation.

If it helps, looping in our counsel now — Marissa (cc'd) — to propose final language. We can also do a 30-minute legal-to-legal sync tomorrow morning.

Next steps I propose: 
- QW legal runs the attached redline and returns comments in-line (ideally by Thu 9/23).
- If comments are heavier, schedule legal-to-legal call Fri 9/24.

Thanks — looking forward to finishing this out.

Thanks, Avery —

Appreciate the clear summary and the targeted redline. A couple of clarifying Qs from legal before we loop in procurement: 

> On Tue, 21 Sep 2026 at 10:04 AM Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Can QuantaWorks confirm whether the primary requirement is an explicit "no training" carve-out for customer data

1) For us, the requirement is that any customer prompts + outputs containing customer confidential data are not used to train Redwood models in a way that would allow that customer data to reappear in other customers' outputs. We can allow aggregated/anonymous telemetry for product metrics, but not training that updates model weights with raw customer content. Is the "training opt-out" language in Section 7.2.A intended to be absolute or conditional on the sensitivity of the data?

2) On feedback license: we need explicit assurance that any feedback we provide (annotated examples, bug reproductions) is only used for product debugging and system-level improvement and cannot be fed into a public or shared training dataset without an explicit separate license.

Timeline: our legal team will review and send in-line comments by COB Thu 9/23. Procurement will want a redline they can push to our vendors team; likely a DocuSign exchange next week if legal signoff is on time.

I'll loop Tom from procurement if we look green after legal review. Thanks for looping Marissa — we'll be in touch.

Emily / QW legal —

Thanks for the quick response and for framing the requirements. I'm Redwood's lead counsel on this engagement; I've gone through the attachment and wrote two alternative clauses in the redline (attached) so you can pick the level of restriction you need. Summary below; see doc for line numbers.

Summary of proposed options
A) Strict opt-out (cleanest for customers): 
- Clause: Redwood will not use any Customer Content (including prompts, outputs, or uploaded files) to perform model weight updates or as training data for models that are made available to other customers, except where Customer has provided a separate, written training license.
- Telemetry: telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are permitted for system monitoring and bug fixing; telemetry will be processed to remove PII and Customer-identifiers.
- Feedback: feedback (bug reports, annotated examples) is licensed to Redwood on a limited, non-exclusive basis solely for debugging and product improvement; explicit consent is required for retraining or inclusion in shared training corpora.

B) Narrowed opt-out (allows aggregated research): 
- Clause: Redwood will not use Customer Confidential Content for model weight updates. Non-confidential, de-identified prompts/outputs may be used for research and model improvement provided they are aggregated and cannot be traced to the Customer.
- Rationale: gives QW assurance on confidential data while preserving Redwood's ability to improve models from broad signals.

Practical notes and operational guardrails (suggested SOW/OPS addendum):
- Process: any request to use customer material for retraining must go through a documented approval workflow with the customer (SOW addendum + explicit written consent).
- Evidence: we can provide attestations of data handling and a periodic summary of telemetry categories used for product improvements.
- Security: integration with customer KMS for key-managed artifacts if QW wants to push cryptographic separation for sensitive uploads.

I attached QW_MSA_Redline_v3.docx with the redline + a short redline_summary.xlsx that maps each proposed sentence to sections and operational checks. Line references are included. If QW prefers Option A, we'll mark the change final and Redwood's C-suite will approve; Option B will need a short SOW addendum in case of future retraining activities.

Next steps:
- If QW legal provides in-line comments by COB 9/23 we can prepare the final DocuSign packet for signature and circulate to procurement.
- If you'd like, schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thu 9/23 11:00 AM PT — I'm available and will include our privacy lead.
